title: Forgiver of sin, accepter of return
hookLine: the surah opens with names: forgiver of sin, accepter of repentance (40:3)

lines: AN INTRODUCTION SAYS WHAT TO EXPECT.
cards: Doctor so-and-so, head of surgery. Judge so-and-so. When you meet someone important, the introduction tells you what to expect, how they'll treat you.
Surah forty begins with an introduction like that. After two opening letters, Ha Mim, and a line saying the book comes from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing, it lists four titles in a row.
The order, and the balance between them, says a great deal about who's being introduced. The first one gives the surah its name.

teach.h: TWO NAMES OF MERCY, ONE OF SEVERITY.
teach.b: Verse three. Pickthall: "The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Stern in punishment, the Bountiful." In Arabic: ghafiri'dh-dhanb, wa qabili't-tawb, shadidi'l-'iqab, dhi't-tawl.
Count them. Two about mercy, then one about severity, then one about generosity. By the time severity is named, mercy has been named twice, and generosity has the last word.
Ghafir comes from a root that means to cover. A mighfar is a helmet, the thing that covers and protects the head. So forgiving, in this word, is covering a sin so that it doesn't harm you.
Qabil at-tawb: the one who accepts the return. Tawb is turning back; qabil is the one who accepts what is brought to him.

Commentators note the two titles are close but not the same: one covers what was done, the other accepts the person who comes back. The verse ends: there is no god but Him, and to Him is the journey, everyone's.
A few verses later comes an image that's easy to miss.
Verse seven: the angels who carry the Throne, and those around it, glorify their Lord and ask forgiveness for the believers.

Our Lord, they say, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who turn back and follow Your way. The surah introduces a Forgiver, then shows angels praying for those who return.
It has two names: some call it Ghafir, the Forgiver, and some call it Al-Mu'min, the Believer, after tomorrow's story.

how: Muslims call on Allah as al-Ghafur and at-Tawwab in their prayers, and many say astaghfirullah repeatedly each day, following the Prophet's practice of seeking forgiveness often.

o: the Judge who weighs every deed
the Forgiver, the One who covers sin
the Guardian who protects the believers

games.q: the four titles in 40:3 — tap the pairs.

s: Surah Ghafir opens with severity before mercy
two names of mercy come first, then one of severity, then generosity.
the root of ghafir is linked to covering, as in a helmet
a mighfar is a helmet: forgiving covers and protects.
in the same surah, angels ask forgiveness for those who turn back
verse seven: the Throne-bearers pray for them.

games.q: Surah Ghafir introduces Allah with four titles. which comes first?
games.why: the Forgiver of sin, then the Accepter of return, and only then severe in punishment, with the Bountiful last.

practice: Choose one specific thing, not your whole life, just one, that you'd like to turn back from, and name it to yourself honestly.
If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah, I ask Allah's forgiveness, and picture the turning being accepted; if not, decide one way to set it right. Then sit in the quiet after the turning.

wordCard.voice: Ghafir, the Forgiver, the first of four titles opening Surah Ghafir, the One who covers sin before it can do harm. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Forgiver of sin and the Accepter of return (40:3).

carryVoice: Your line: he accepts the return. Two names of mercy come before one of severity. That's day five hundred sixty-one.
